summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic myeloid leukemia s/p stem cell transplant, chronic GVHD, diabetes, and prior DVT/PE was admitted for a non-healing left leg ulcer and antibiotic-associated diarrhea. She had sustained a leg injury 22 days prior, and despite oral antibiotics, the wound failed to heal. Diarrhea developed on doxycycline but resolved after discontinuation. On admission, she was started on vancomycin, but it was discontinued on hospital day 2 due to lack of infection signs and negative wound culture. A bedside debridement was performed to remove necrotic tissue impeding healing. IVIG was given for low IgG levels. Her pain was managed with oral hydromorphone, and she was discharged home with wound care instructions, a short course of pain medication, and follow-up planned. Weight loss was attributed to recent poor intake from gastrointestinal symptoms.
